newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russian debt term sheet well received-Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt term sheet well received-Deutsche.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Friday that financing proposals for an agreed rescheduling of Russian debt had received a good welcome from creditor banks.

Deutsche, which chairs the bank advisory committee for the so-called London club of creditor banks, said a preliminary evaluation showed that banks had given commitments for an aggregate principal amount of 20 billion dollars.
"These claims are currently being analysed with a view to their reconciliation," Deutsche said in a statement.

Russia and its creditor banks reached agreement last November to reschedule the repayment of $25.5 billion in principal over a 25-year period and $7 billion in interest arrears over 20 years, both with a seven-year grace period.
The statement said the financing proposals for the rescheduling, the so-called term sheet, had been "well received."
Creditors were requested to commit to the terms of the restructuring by forwarding their claims to the Reconciliation Office in Moscow by August 27.

"According to information provided to Deutsche Bank AG by the Reconciliation Office, a preliminary evaluation of the commitment messages shows that commitments for an aggregate principal amount exceeding 20 billion U.S. dollars (or its equivalent in other currencies) have been received," the statement said.
Russian officials have said they expect Russia's 600 creditor banks to give final agreement to the rescheduling of Russian debt in late autumn this year.
Final agreement on debt rescheduling will pave the way for Russia to tap the international capital market with a dollar-based Eurobond.
